findings.evidence: template/scripts/execute_requirement.py:726-735: the `materialize_handoff` loop (727-732) and `read_platform_config` run before `_require_no_merged_composition` at 735. design.md line 8 says 'The check runs first'. The spec only requires the refusal before the integration branch is touched, so the requirement holds, but design and code differ.
findings.summary: Design says the refusal check runs first in `_advance_contributions`, but it runs after handoff materialization, so a refused advance can still create linked child Issues.

findings.evidence: design.md line 8: '`gh pr list --state all --head <branch> --base main` inventory ... any merged PR of the branch refuses'. The code at execute_requirement.py:176 passes `--state merged`. The behavior matches the spec, but the 100-item bound now applies to merged PRs only, and the design text is stale.
findings.summary: Design describes the inventory as `--state all` and refuses on any merged PR. The code lists only `--state merged`.

findings.evidence: execute_requirement.py:190-191 builds `work-next --repo {repository} --kinds ... --pr {first} --run`. design.md line 9 names `work-next --kinds retrospective,terminal-reconciliation,cleanup --pr N`. Minor documentation drift; the spec requires only that the coordinator's post-merge jobs and the status command are named.
findings.summary: The suggested post-merge command includes `--repo` and `--run`, which design.md and the spec text do not mention.
